top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is a distinct, original idea (state-independent trapping of many neutral atoms on a narrow transition, cancelling light shifts and Doppler and recoil effects) that took frequency measurement to the 10^-18 level and is reproduced in several laboratories, with applications in tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy. It is separable from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 single-ion prize if the citation is worded around the lattice concept. The Katori and Ye allocation is defensible, though I cannot verify the strontium versus ytterbium first-demonstration history and credit to Takamoto, Hong, Ludlow, Lemke and others remains a residual concern. It is mature enough that an award is preferable to no award.
